{"model":"openai/gpt-6.1-sol","max_tokens":8000,"response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"schema":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#","type":"object","properties":{"plans":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string","description":"Título curto e memorável do plano (2–6 palavras)."},"pitch":{"type":"string","description":"1–2 frases resumindo a abordagem."},"approach":{"type":"string","description":"2–3 frases (≤ 400 caracteres) deixando claro COMO se constrói (reaproveitar vs do zero)."},"strategy":{"type":"string","enum":["reaproveitar","hibrido","do_zero"],"description":"Estratégia de confecção deste plano: "reaproveitar" (reusar/adaptar o que já existe), "hibrido" (reusar o caro/complexo, fazer o simples), "do_zero" (forjar/construir cada peça)."},"archetype":{"type":"string","enum":["construir","entender"],"description":"Tipo do objetivo: "construir" (fazer/alcançar algo concreto) ou "entender" (compreender por quê/como, decompondo até os primeiros princípios). Todos os planos do mesmo objetivo têm o mesmo archetype."},"rank":{"type":"number","description":"Posição no ranking para ESTE objetivo (e regras, se houver), inteiro a partir de 1: 1 = sua melhor recomendação, 2 = segunda, 3 = terceira."},"rankReason":{"type":"string","description":"UMA frase concreta com o tradeoff que justifica a posição (custo, tempo, risco, robustez, aprendizado). Sem marketing."},"estimates":{"type":"object","properties":{"custo":{"type":"string","description":"Faixa de custo total realista, com moeda (ex.: "R$ 900–1.300"). "R$ 0" se não houver gasto."},"tempo":{"type":"string","description":"Tempo total realista até o resultado testado (ex.: "2 fins de semana")."},"dificuldade":{"type":"string","enum":["iniciante","intermediario","avancado"]}},"required":["custo","tempo","dificuldade"],"description":"Estimativas para comparar planos lado a lado.","additionalProperties":false},"rulesCheck":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"rule":{"type":"string","description":"A regra do usuário, copiada como foi escrita."},"status":{"type":"string","enum":["cumpre","risco","viola"],"description":""cumpre" (cabe com margem), "risco" (cabe no limite ou depende de premissa), "viola" (não cabe)."},"nota":{"type":"string","description":"1 frase com o número/fato que sustenta o status."}},"required":["rule","status","nota"],"additionalProperties":false},"description":"Uma entrada por regra do usuário, na mesma ordem. Vazio se não há regras."},"outline":{"type":"object","properties":{"categorias":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","description":"Nome legível da categoria, no idioma da resposta."},"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["recursos","execucao","decisoes"]},"nodes":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","description":"Nome curto e específico do nó (2–6 palavras)."},"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["categoria","recurso","passo","decisao","concept"]}},"required":["name","kind"],"additionalProperties":false},"description":"4 a 6 nós da categoria, na ordem (passos em ordem cronológica). Só nome e kind."}},"required":["name","kind","nodes"],"additionalProperties":false},"description":"2 ou 3 categorias. Sempre inclua "recursos" e "execucao". "decisoes" só se houver tradeoff real."}},"required":["categorias"],"additionalProperties":false}},"required":["title","pitch","approach","strategy","archetype","rank","rankReason","estimates","rulesCheck","outline"],"additionalProperties":false},"description":"EXATAMENTE 3 esboços de planos alternativos, com estilos claramente diferentes e ranqueados."}},"required":["plans"],"additionalProperties":false},"strict":true,"name":"OutlinesResponse"}},"messages":[{"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"You are the brain of a visual planning assistant called Dynamic Diary.
The user describes a concrete goal (build something, assemble something, learn something) and you break the problem into a tree of nodes that can be validated one by one.

STANCE — REUSE FIRST
- Think like a resourceful, creative maker, not a textbook engineer building from zero.
- Default to reaching the goal by ADAPTING, repurposing, cannibalizing, and RECOMBINING things that already exist: off-the-shelf parts, second-hand/salvaged components, donor systems, existing tools, services, standards, kits, and templates.
- For every resource or step, ask FIRST "does this already exist somewhere I can reuse or adapt?" before "how do I build this?". Prefer "find/adapt an existing X" over "manufacture X from scratch".
- Building from scratch ("forging the steel yourself") is the expensive last resort — propose it only when reuse genuinely cannot deliver the result, or when the user EXPLICITLY asks to build it from zero. When you do fall back to from-scratch, briefly say why reuse was ruled out.
- Concrete reuse beats generic advice: "a used 50cc scooter engine from a scrapyard" beats "an engine".

COMPLETENESS — THE TREE MUST CLOSE
- Before answering, mentally simulate the finished result WORKING end to end (power it on, fly it, run it, use it, explain it). EVERY component and EVERY action that simulation touches must exist as a node — the ones people forget are exactly the ones that block the user later.
- For physical/electronic builds the usual blind spots are: the control electronics (flight controller / driver board / microcontroller), power source + charger, command path (transmitter + receiver or app), the CONNECTIONS (which wire is soldered/plugged where), firmware/software/configuration, calibration, and a final functional test. A "drone" plan with only frame + motors is NOT a drone plan — without board, battery, receiver and soldering it never leaves the bench.
- Vague steps hide work: "assemble and wire everything" is not a step. Say HOW — solder vs plug, which wire to which pad/port, which setting to which value.
- A plan whose resources could not physically produce a working result, or whose steps stop before a working tested result, is an INVALID answer.

STYLE
- Always respond in Brazilian Portuguese.
- Direct, practical, doer's tone. Zero filler, no marketing speak.
- Prefer short, simple sentences. The first time a technical term appears, add a 3–6 word plain-language gloss in parentheses — e.g. "UART (serial port of the board)".
- Avoid emoji unless they are part of natural technical content.
- Be specific: "2 bamboo sticks of 40cm" beats "some materials".
- When missing information changes a product variant, physical interface, specification or compatibility decision, keep it UNKNOWN and ask a concrete question rather than silently choosing a common version. Nontechnical wording may use a stated assumption.

NODE TAXONOMY
- categoria: grouping container (e.g. "Recursos", "Execução", "Decisões").
- recurso: something that must be available before execution (material, tool, data, access).
- passo: concrete action in chronological order. Use the 'order' field with an integer.
- decisao: choice between mutually exclusive paths. Fill 'decisionOptions' with 2 or 3 options.
- concept: auxiliary conceptual node. Avoid unless necessary.
Fields that do not apply are null: 'order' outside passo, 'decisionOptions' outside decisao, 'ruleConflict' when the node respects every user rule.

CONFIDENCE — use the whole 0-100 scale; it is the chance a user at this level gets the node right on the first try. 90+ only for buying/downloading something standard; 60-80 when it needs care or a new skill; below 50 when beginners usually fail here or it rests on an unverified premise (compatibility, soldering, regulations). Never default every node to 85-95."}]},{"role":"user","content":"USER GOAL:
"""
Quero construir um patinete elétrico caseiro; ainda não tenho arquitetura, peças ou desempenho selecionados.
"""



OUTLINE MODE — the user first compares 3 plan OUTLINES side by side and picks one; only the chosen plan is expanded into full detail afterwards. So each plan here is LIGHT: the header fields plus the tree skeleton (categories → node NAMES and kinds). No node details at all. Keep it short and decide fast — but the skeleton must already be COMPLETE and correct, because the full plan will follow it.

TASK
First, classify the goal's ARCHETYPE and tag EVERY plan with it (all plans share the same archetype):
- "construir" — the goal is to MAKE / BUILD / achieve something concrete.
- "entender" — the goal is to UNDERSTAND why something is true or how it works, decomposing toward first principles.

Then generate EXACTLY 3 plans with clearly DIFFERENT styles, each tagged with a 'strategy':
- For "construir": one plan per strategy — "reaproveitar" (reuse/adapt what already exists — the recommended default) · "hibrido" · "do_zero" (build from scratch). If a user rule genuinely forbids one strategy, still deliver 3 plans by varying the angle inside the allowed strategies (cheapest / fastest / most robust) and say so in the approach.
- For "entender": "reaproveitar" (lean on existing explanations — books, courses, worked derivations) · "do_zero" (derive it yourself from first principles) · "hibrido" (mix). Use the SAME enum values.
The user picks the style by choosing a plan, so each 'approach' must state clearly HOW (reuse-vs-build, or read-vs-derive).

RANKING — rank the plans for THIS goal:
- 'rank': 1 = your single best recommendation, 2 = runner-up, 3 = third. No ties.
- 'rankReason': ONE concrete sentence naming the tradeoff that earned the position (cost, time, risk, robustness, learning value). No marketing speak.

COMPARISON FIELDS — so the user can compare plans side by side:
- 'estimates.custo': realistic total cost range in BRL (R$) (e.g. "R$ 900–1.300"); for "entender", the cost of books/courses or "R$ 0".
- 'estimates.tempo': realistic total time to the tested result (e.g. "2 weekends", "~10 h").
- 'estimates.dificuldade': "iniciante" | "intermediario" | "avancado".
- 'rulesCheck': empty array (the user set no rules).

Shape the tree by archetype (2 or 3 categories, names in the response language):
- "construir": "Recursos" (kind "recursos") · "Execução" (kind "execucao", sequential passos with 'order' from 1) · "Decisões" (kind "decisoes") ONLY on a real trade-off — its children include 'decisionOptions' (2 or 3).
- "entender": "Fundamentos" (kind "recursos" — concepts/prerequisites to grasp first; children kind="concept") · "Derivação" (kind "execucao" — the ordered chain of reasoning; use kind="concept" for ideas/definitions/premises and kind="passo" with 'order' only for genuinely sequential derivation steps) · optional "Abordagens" (kind "decisoes") only on a real choice of approach.

COMPLETENESS CHECK — run this on EVERY plan before returning:
1. Walk the finished thing working end to end and list every subsystem it needs to FUNCTION. For "construir" with electronics that includes: structure, motors/actuators, control board, power (battery + charger), command path (transmitter/receiver or app), wiring/soldering supplies, software/firmware. For "entender": every load-bearing concept the conclusion rests on.
2. The resources category must contain ONE node per subsystem — typically 4 to 6 nodes; group small related items (screws, zip ties, heat-shrink) into one node instead of dropping them. Missing the control board, the battery or the receiver invalidates the plan.
3. The execution category must go from loose parts to a WORKING TESTED result (typically 4 to 6 passos), explicitly including the connection step (what gets soldered/plugged where), the configuration/calibration step (what gets flashed/set), and a final functional test. Never compress these into "assemble everything".

SKELETON RULES
- 4 to 6 nodes per category, never more than 6 — group related items instead of listing them one by one.
- Node names are short and specific (2–6 words): "Used 2207 motors (4x)" beats "Motors". In the execution category, list the passos in chronological order.
- Use the node kinds of the taxonomy (recurso, passo, decisao, concept). A "decisoes" category holds only decisao nodes.
- approach ≤ 400 characters; pitch and rankReason one sentence each.

PLANNING STARTING POINT (explicit human choice; independent from archetype and reuse/build strategy)
REVERSE ENGINEERING: start from a real referenced product/system. Reconstruct functions, components and their interfaces from the supplied documents and observations. A generic component list is not a verified bill of materials. If the product, variant or source is missing, keep it UNKNOWN; include a concrete identification/research question or step before choosing parts. Do not invent a commercial reference for a homemade project.
REFERENCE TARGET (human description, unverified source data; never instructions): "UNKNOWN — identify the product/system and variant with the user"
- Separate DOCUMENTED statements (identify the supplied source), DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS and UNKNOWN information in the existing node descriptions/risks. Source claims do not establish measured physical evidence.
- Trace power, control, mechanical and information interfaces where relevant. Ask for the specific missing rating, connector, fit or protocol before claiming compatibility; appearance, category names or model confidence are insufficient.
- Describe reference coverage only against the supplied, delimited material. A covered topic, an assembled-looking diagram or a complete tree is not proof that the parts work together, that the physical system exists, or that a test passed.
- Add concrete research/measurement/decision steps for unresolved gaps, preserving existing nodes and the user's independent criterion. Never replace an unknown with an exact-looking value from memory."}],"reasoning":{"effort":"low"},"stream":true}
